basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 28.' and it opens '(Vers. 28.) Judam vero misit ante se ad Joseph, ut occurreret ei ad urbem Heroum in'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 28.) Judam vero misit ante se ad Joseph, ut occurreret ei ad urbem Heroum in terram Ramesse. In Hebraeo nec urbem habet Heroum, nec terram Ramesse, sed tantummodo Gesen. Nonnulli Judaeorum asserunt, Gesen nunc Thebaidem vocari. Et id quod postea sequitur: Dedit eis, ut possiderent Aegypti [Al. in Aegypto] optimam terram in Ramesse, pagum Arsenoitem sic olim vocatum autumant.
